primary_diagnosis_treated: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) with proteinuria, hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, anaemia
nice_guideline_used: NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.duration: Existing – continue only until switch to atorvastatin
medications.nice_justification: Statin therapy recommended for all CKD patients (NG203)

medications.purpose: High‑intensity lipid lowering for cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends high‑intensity statin (e.g., atorvastatin 20 mg) for CKD patients

medications.duration: Start 2.5 mg, titrate to 10 mg over 8‑12 weeks as tolerated, then lifelong – review annually
medications.purpose: Renoprotective ACE‑I for proteinuric CKD and hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203: ACE‑I/ARB first‑line for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine & K⁺

medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive to achieve BP <130/80 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NG203: combination therapy (ACE‑I + CCB) recommended when BP target not met

medications.dose: 200 mg PO once daily (≈65 mg elemental iron)
medications.duration: Until ferritin >200 µg/L and TSAT >20 %, then review
medications.purpose: Treat iron deficiency anaemia of CKD (pending iron studies)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Iron supplementation for CKD anaemia when ferritin/TSAT low

medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L, then review
medications.purpose: Correct metabolic acidosis if bicarbonate <20 mmol/L
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Sodium bicarbonate for CKD patients with metabolic acidosis

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering (desired); monitor for hypotension and electrolytes
interactions_checked.action: Start low dose Ramipril, check BP and renal function after 1‑2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: CYP3A4 competition may increase simvastatin levels
interactions_checked.action: Switch to atorvastatin (less interaction) and discontinue simvastatin
Titrate slowly, monitor BP and renal function

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential shift of potassium intracellularly; monitor serum K⁺

contraindications.reason: eGFR 15 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis (NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or GLP‑1 receptor agonist (if not contraindicated)

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and AKI (NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Use ACE‑I alone (Ramipril) or ARB if ACE‑I intolerant

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – measurement required before adding Amlodipine.
Serum potassium level not available – baseline needed prior to ACE‑I initiation.
Liver function tests not available – baseline required before starting atorvastatin.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) and haemoglobin not available – needed to confirm iron deficiency before iron supplementation or ESA.
Serum bicarbonate not available – required to confirm metabolic acidosis before sodium bicarbonate.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statins, sulfonamides not documented – verify before prescribing.
Current diabetes medication regimen not provided – ensure metformin is stopped and appropriate glucose‑lowering therapy instituted.
treatment_summary: Switch low‑intensity simvastatin to high‑intensity atorvastatin, initiate low‑dose ramipril with careful renal and potassium monitoring, add amlodipine if BP remains above target, address CKD‑related anaemia with oral iron (pending iron studies) and correct metabolic acidosis with sodium bicarbonate if needed. Avoid metformin, NSAIDs, and ACE‑I/ARB combination. Monitor BP, eGFR, electrolytes, liver enzymes, iron parameters, and bicarbonate at 1‑2 weeks after each change and then at routine intervals per NG203.
